text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Opposition Centre Party leader Esko Aho dropped out of the running for presidency of Nordic Council because Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen would not support him.
- Finland's membership in the European Economic and Monetary Union should be decided by a simple parliamentary majority, said Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto.
- Drunkeness among schoolchildren growing widespread. Ten percent of 14-year-olds say they get drunk over twice a week. @
- Transport workers union AKT threatening to halt fuelling aircraft next week in an action to support airport bus drivers' pay demands.
KAUPPALEHTI

- Kesko Oy CEO Eero Kinnunen says the company would prefer to find a Finnish buyer for Tuko rather than a foreign one. Several former Tuko owners are known to be interested in buying back their Tuko stakes.
- Economics professor John Kenneth Galbraith, on a visit to Finland, said that preserving the welfare state should take precedence to the common European currency. @
- World's second largest air freight forwarder MSAS Cargo International stepping up operations in Finland -- says Nokia accounts for 75 percent of its business here.
- Finnish fur farmers producing a record volume of blue fox hides this year. Fur dealer Turkistuottajat Oy will hold extra auction in November to destock.
DEMARI
- Social Democrat MPs elected Erkki Tuomioja new parliamentary group leader -- to succeed Pertti Paasio who was elected to the European Parliament. @
AAMULEHTI
- Consumers rated service provided by various service-sector organisations and found car road worthiness inspectors led the pack.
- Museum exhibition to show wood- and paper-made shoes.
- Finnish centre will be first in Nordic region to begin collecting placenta blood next year. Blood from the placenta is known to cure many blood diseases.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Finnyards shop steward said Thursday's shareholders' meeting had dispelled fears of a quick closure of the yard, but he had hoped for news of new ship orders. @
